title: Horse Neigh
blurb: A full-throated neigh, complete with the rising whinny at the end. Horses make this noise chiefly to reach each other across distance, so it carries absurdly well and works even better as an interruption. Radio comedians worked that out early and the trick never wore off. Play it after a bad pun, over a slow-motion entrance, or any time somebody says something that deserves to be answered by livestock rather than by people. The horse has no notes on your material. The horse simply objects.
origin: A field recording of a horse whinnying.
